solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Possible putter’s line for nineteenth hole? (9)

blocks.note: a putter is one of the clubs a golfer might use
a line of descent, as in the House of Windsor

annotation.surface: A golfer wonders what excuse to offer in the bar after the round.
annotation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes 'line' the path a putt takes, but it is a royal line. The nineteenth hole is golfers' slang for the bar, which sits in the clubhouse.
annotation.definitionFit: The nineteenth hole is the jokey name for the golf clubhouse bar, where players go after the eighteenth.

entries.clue: Disgraced arboretum cut down tree (5)

indicatorNotes.cut down: the two words are trimmed down to a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join: disgraCED ARboretum

annotation.surface: A disgraced arboretum has had a tree felled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut down tree' reads as felling, but 'cut down' tells you to trim the first two words to what sits across their join.
annotation.definitionFit: The cedar is a large evergreen conifer.

entries.clue: What comforts party perhaps as following disappears (7)

indicatorNotes.disappears: the letter for 'following' goes missing from the word

blocks.note: a function is a party or formal gathering
f. = following, the abbreviation used in page references; this is the letter that disappears from the front of the party

annotation.surface: Someone takes comfort at a party as their followers drift away.
annotation.walkthrough: Unction is anointing with oil, and by extension anything soothing, which is why 'What comforts' can stand for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Unction is an anointing or soothing ointment, so something that comforts.

entries.clue: Shark acted horribly eating bird not flying away (10)

indicatorNotes.eating: the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: to ham it up is to act badly and overdo it
the rhea is a flightless South American bird, so it cannot fly away

annotation.surface: A shark overacts while devouring a bird that failed to escape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not flying away' reads as the bird being caught, but it describes the bird itself: the rhea cannot fly.
annotation.definitionFit: The hammerhead is a shark with a flattened, hammer-shaped head.

entries.clue: Tune’s fragments not yet composed (5)

indicatorNotes.fragments: the tune's letters are broken into pieces and put back in another order

blocks.note: the letters of TUNES rearranged

annotation.surface: Scraps of a tune lie around, not yet worked into a finished piece.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'composed' mean written, but it means set in type, as a compositor sets type.
annotation.definitionFit: Type that has not been composed is unset, not yet set up for printing.

entries.clue: Make a mistake with my delivery person (6,3)

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
and = with
'my!' and 'boy!' are both exclamations of surprise

annotation.surface: A courier admits to a mistake with a delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive attached to 'delivery person', but it is the exclamation 'my!', which BOY also is.
annotation.definitionFit: An errand boy runs errands, carrying messages and parcels.

entries.clue: Conclude Dawn has had a change of heart (3,2)

indicators: has had a change of heart

indicatorNotes.has had a change of heart: the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

blocks.note: sunup is dawn; its central N is changed to M

annotation.surface: A woman named Dawn has changed her mind.
annotation.walkthrough: Dawn reads as a woman's name, but it is sunrise. The new middle letter M is not clued, so the definition must supply it.
annotation.definitionFit: To sum up is to conclude, giving a final summary.

entries.clue: Fish in shoal he’s regularly taken (4)

indicatorNotes.regularly taken: every other letter is picked out

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of S h O a L h E s

annotation.surface: A fisherman regularly takes a fish from a shoal.
annotation.walkthrough: The fishing surface makes 'regularly taken' sound like a catch, but it tells you to take alternate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the sole is a common European flatfish, so plain 'fish' covers it.

entries.clue: Physicist, the most significant one by a considerable margin (7)

blocks.note: max, short for maximum, is the greatest one
as in 'well ahead' or 'well over'

annotation.surface: A tribute naming one physicist the greatest by a long way.
annotation.walkthrough: James Clerk Maxwell was the Scottish physicist who unified electricity and magnetism, so the surface's praise is not far off.
annotation.definitionFit: James Clerk Maxwell was a 19th-century physicist famed for his equations of electromagnetism.

entries.clue: Measuring device’s safe when put round head (9)

indicatorNotes.put round: the safe is placed around the head

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
dome is slang for the head

annotation.surface: A measuring instrument is protected once fitted around someone's head.
annotation.walkthrough: PETER is underworld slang for a safe, as in 'peterman', a safe-cracker.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedometer measures how far you walk by counting steps.

entries.clue: In final months current unit leaves temporary base (7)

indicatorNotes.In: the unit goes inside the months

blocks.note: the amp is the unit of electric current
Dec. is December, the final month of the year; plural DECS

annotation.surface: In the last months of the year a military unit pulls out of its temporary camp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current unit' reads as today's regiment, but current means electric current.
annotation.definitionFit: To decamp is literally to leave a camp, a temporary base.

entries.clue: Easygoing unknown replacing another in broadcast (7)

indicatorNotes.replacing: one unknown takes the place of the other

blocks.note: to relay is to broadcast
y is another algebraic unknown, the letter removed
x is the unknown in algebra, put in its place

annotation.surface: A laid-back presenter is swapped in for someone else on air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' only makes sense once 'unknown' is read as algebra: the unknowns are x and y, so another one is Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Relaxed and easygoing both mean calm and unfussed.

entries.clue: Fake gem and nine others needing resetting (10)

indicatorNotes.needing resetting: the letters must be set in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of NINE OTHERS rearranged

annotation.surface: A jeweller has a fake stone and nine more that must be remounted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resetting' belongs to the jeweller's picture of setting stones, but here it rearranges letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond made of glass or paste.

entries.clue: Fantasise removing last of bed sheets (4)

indicatorNotes.removing: to remove something is to take it off, so the last letter of 'bed' is taken off the fantasy

blocks.note: to dream is to fantasise
the last letter of beD, removed from the front of DREAM

annotation.surface: Someone lies fantasising after stripping the bed sheets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bed sheets' reads as bedding, but the phrase splits: 'bed' feeds the wordplay and 'sheets' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, traditionally 500 sheets.

entries.clue: Sweet spirit of murdered Colm O’Neill (10)

indicatorNotes.murdered: the name is mangled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of COLM ONEILL rearranged

annotation.surface: The gentle ghost of a murdered man called Colm O'Neill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' leans on the murder to suggest a ghost, but it is a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Limoncello is a sweet Italian lemon liqueur.

entries.clue: Suspicion of hot meal that’s left out (5)

indicatorNotes.that’s left out: the meal with its L, for left, taken out

blocks.note: h = hot, as on a tap
lunch is a meal; without L it is UNCH

annotation.surface: Someone suspects a hot meal has been forgotten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as omitted, but it means the letter for left is taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a feeling you cannot prove, like a suspicion, is a gut feeling of the same kind.

entries.clue: String up individual losing power and followers (7-2)

indicatorNotes.losing: the letter for power is dropped

blocks.note: to string up is to hang
an individual is a person
p = power, removed from PERSON to leave ERSON

annotation.surface: A mob strings up someone who has lost both power and supporters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And followers' reads as part of what the individual loses, but 'and' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are followers who attach themselves to someone for gain.

entries.clue: Cold dash in a hired car having unfixed roof (9)

blocks.note: c = cold, as on a tap
the word itself
brio is dash, verve
a property that is let is hired out

annotation.surface: A chilly dash in a rented car with a loose roof.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A hired car' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'a hired' holds the dash, and 'car' starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the folding hood of this convertible body style is the roof that is not fixed.

entries.clue: Scream about husband I punish for deceitfulness (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the scream goes around the rest

blocks.note: to cry out is to scream
h = husband, as in genealogy tables
the word itself
to cane is to punish with a stick

annotation.surface: A wife screams at her husband, vowing to punish him for lying.
annotation.walkthrough: The domestic row reads as a sentence, but each word is a separate piece dropped inside CRY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word first meant legal trickery and quibbling, and has widened to any deceitful dealing.

entries.clue: Royal Mint’s working in the usual way (9)

annotation.definitionNote: normality is a state rather than a way of doing things; 'in the usual way' loosely paraphrases 'in normality'

indicatorNotes.working: the letters are worked into a new shape

blocks.note: the letters of ROYAL MINT rearranged

annotation.surface: The Royal Mint is carrying on business as usual.
annotation.walkthrough: The Royal Mint is the UK body that makes coins. 'Working' reads as being open for business, but it rearranges the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose paraphrase: 'in normality' would mean in the ordinary state of things, which the clue words as 'in the usual way'.

entries.clue: Theatre building’s top carpeting (7)

blocks.note: rep = repertory theatre
the roof is the top of a building

annotation.surface: A theatre's upper floor is having new carpets laid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like floor covering, but a carpeting is a British word for a telling-off, from being called onto the boss's carpet.
annotation.definitionFit: A carpeting is a severe scolding, which is what a reproof is.

entries.clue: Very big vehicle, coveted model of stars (5)

blocks.note: OS = outsize, a clothing label
a car is a vehicle

annotation.surface: A huge vehicle, a sought-after model among celebrities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a make of car to match 'vehicle', but it is a statuette, and the stars are film stars.
annotation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the gold statuette film stars covet at the Academy Awards.

entries.clue: Bread with bit of butter I had after tea (7)

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter
the word itself

annotation.surface: A snack of bread and butter taken after a cup of tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' reads as eating, but it only says the butter and I come after the tea.
annotation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

entries.clue: See psychic ability decay finally (4)

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the end, so only the end of 'decay' is used

blocks.note: ESP = extrasensory perception
the last letter of decaY

annotation.surface: Look how a clairvoyant's powers fade in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as an order to look at what follows, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly literary: to catch sight of something at a distance.

entries.clue: Creative work? Hard in fact to be new (10)

indicatorNotes.to be new: the letters are to be made into something new

blocks.note: the letters of HARD IN FACT rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone finds that original creative work is hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard' looks like the letter H going inside something, but the whole phrase 'Hard in fact' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Handicraft is skilled work made by hand, a creative craft.

entries.clue: Former barrister’s assistant was on the way up (5)

indicatorNotes.on the way up: in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: lived = existed, was

annotation.surface: A former clerk to a barrister was climbing the career ladder.
annotation.walkthrough: In British law, a devil is a junior barrister who does work for a senior one; 'former' flags that the usage is old.
annotation.definitionFit: A devil was a junior barrister who did work for a more senior one.

entries.clue: Right leaving hem in skimpy garment (5)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the letter for right goes away

blocks.note: r = right, the letter removed
to throng is to crowd around, hem in

annotation.surface: A seamstress takes a hem in on a skimpy outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: The sewing picture makes 'hem in' mean taking up a hem, but it means to crowd in, THRONG.
annotation.definitionFit: A thong is a very skimpy piece of underwear or swimwear.

entries.clue: Half of fish can be bleak in Chesapeake Bay (4)

indicatorNotes.Half of: keep only the first half of the word

blocks.note: the grayling is a freshwater fish; keep its first four letters

annotation.surface: Half the fish in Chesapeake Bay are having a bad time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bleak' is itself a fish, so it looks like the fish, but here it means dreary. Chesapeake Bay is in the US, which calls for the American spelling GRAY.
annotation.definitionFit: Gray, the American spelling of grey, means dull and bleak.

entries.clue: Flog company during sudden upswing (7)

indicatorNotes.during: the company sits within the upswing

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rise
Co. = company

annotation.surface: Sell off a firm while its shares are suddenly rising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as British slang for sell, which fits the business picture, but it means whip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scourge was a whip, and the verb means to beat with one.

entries.clue: Potential hazard to life volunteer is able to duck (7)

blocks.note: vol. = volunteer
can = is able to
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: A volunteer who can dodge a threat to life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' reads as a verb for dodging, but it is the cricket score of zero, O.
annotation.definitionFit: An active volcano can erupt and threaten life around it.

entries.clue: N + L – F? Neat (5)

indicatorNotes.+: the plus sign means add, so N is added to the number written as a word
indicatorNotes.–: the minus sign means subtract, so F is taken out of that word, and N fills the gap

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the first F of FIFTY, taken away
the letter itself, added in its place

annotation.surface: A tidy little formula that looks like algebra.
annotation.walkthrough: The formula looks like letter arithmetic, but L must first become the word FIFTY before the sum works.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the informal sense: a neat trick or a nifty gadget is deft and clever.

entries.clue: Shouting around old wife visibly ageing (9)

indicatorNotes.around: the shouting goes around the other letters

blocks.note: yelling is shouting
o = old
w = wife

annotation.surface: A man shouts at his old wife, who is showing her age.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old wife' reads as one person, but it splits into O and W.
annotation.definitionFit: Paper, teeth and old photographs yellow as they age, so yellowing is visible ageing.
